claim:
Consider a fully mixed population of \(N\) agents with \(s\) fixed initial seeds and independent thresholds uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,N\}\) for all other agents, each activating permanently when the active count reaches its threshold. For every pair of integers \(1\le s\le k\le N\), the final active count \(K_{N,s}\) satisfies
\[
\Pr(K_{N,s}=k)=\binom{N-s}{k-s}\frac{s\,k^{k-s-1}}{N^{k-s}}\left(1-\frac{k}{N}\right)^{N-k},
\]
with \(0^0=1\); in particular, \(\Pr(K_{N,s}=N)=s/N\). Moreover, for fixed \(s\) and \(\epsilon\in(0,1)\),
\[
\sqrt N\,\Pr(K_{N,s}\ge\lceil\epsilon N\rceil)\longrightarrow s\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\sqrt{\frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}},
\]
and, conditional on that event, \(K_{N,s}/N\) converges in distribution to the density \(\frac{\sqrt{\epsilon}}{2\sqrt{1-\epsilon}}x^{-3/2}(1-x)^{-1/2}\) on \((\epsilon,1)\).

correctness.rationale: The exact mass follows from the generalized parking-function count and independence of the unselected thresholds. The fixed-s tail law follows from an exact mass ratio to the one-seed case, uniform Stirling asymptotics away from the endpoints, an integrable endpoint bound, and the explicitly evaluated integral. The verifier confirms exact normalization and small-population enumeration; these finite checks are corroborative only.

value.rationale: The formula gives the full finite-population distribution for a natural multi-seed intervention, the exact probability \(s/N\) of full mobilization, and the \(N^{-1/2}\) probability and conditional size profile of macroscopic cascades. These risk quantities are not supplied by a mean-size asymptotic and are useful for understanding how seed count changes rare large outcomes.
